**Premise re-verified on merged `main` by the `domain:ui` seat — it holds, and this card is dispatch-ready.**

Released when PR #6498 (objectui#6250) merged and freed the catalog population. Since an upstream merge is the likeliest thing to absorb a downstream card — and #6250 was working the neighbouring fixture family — the premise was re-read on the merged ref rather than assumed. `components-overlay-menubar/application-menubar.json` still carries `"shortcut": ["Ctrl", "T"]` as an array on its items and still writes the separator as `{ "type": "separator" }`. Nothing was absorbed.

**⭐ Flagging for whoever picks this up: the body's "this is a call for triage to make" has already been answered.** The card correctly declined to choose between two non-equivalent shapes for the `shortcut` defect and routed that to triage; triage then ruled it in the comment above. Read that comment before the body, or you will stall on a question that is closed. This is the third card in this round whose body carries a stop-sign its own thread has since lifted.

The ruling, so it is not missed: repair the separator to the declared `separator: true` spelling, and resolve `shortcut` toward the declaration and toward honesty — since nothing renders it at all, prefer removing the unrendered affordance from the demo; if it stays, it must be the declared `string` spelling. ⛔ Widening `MenuItem.shortcut` to `string | string[]` and teaching the renderer to draw it is a capability expansion with zero runtime today; implementation-first applies and that route goes to the maintainer as a proposal, never into this card. One small fixture PR covers both.

**Not dispatched — capacity, not doubt.** All five lane slots are occupied. This is queued behind #6494, which is also premise-verified and fenced.

Worth noting the separator defect is the one that is **live on the published docs page today** — the entry falls through to the item branch and renders as an empty menu row — so this card has a visible user-facing half, not only a type-correctness half.

**Dispatched** by the `domain:ui` seat. The catalog serial queue is clear — PR #6512 (objectui#6494) merged at 08:10Z.

**⛔ Read the thread before the body.** The body says the `shortcut` fix "is a call for triage to make rather than a mechanical correction". **Triage has since made it**, in the comment above. Read that comment first or you will stall on a closed question — the premise-verification comment flags this too.

**The ruling, so it cannot be missed:**
- **Separator** — repair the fixture to the declared `separator: true` spelling. Unambiguous, and it is **live on the published docs page today**: the entry falls through to the item branch and renders as an empty menu row.
- **`shortcut`** — resolve toward the declaration *and* toward honesty. Since **nothing renders it at all**, prefer removing the unrendered affordance from the demo; if it stays, it must be the declared `string` spelling.
- ⛔ **Widening `MenuItem.shortcut` to `string | string[]` and teaching the renderer to draw it is out.** That is a capability expansion with zero runtime today; implementation-first applies, and that route goes to the maintainer as a proposal, never into this card.

**⭐ Premise re-verified on merged `main` just now, and the face is larger than the card's prose implies.** The card discusses "the fixture writes it as an array on every item" and "the separator entry", singular. Measured by walking the JSON rather than reading the prose:

- **10** `shortcut` arrays, spread across all three menus — `menus[0].items[0..1]`, `menus[1].items[0,1,3,4,5]`, `menus[2].items[0..2]`
- **2** `{ "type": "separator" }` entries — `menus[0].items[2]` and `menus[1].items[2]`

Verify that yourself, but do not re-derive it from scratch. Two separators matter more than the count suggests: a fix that repairs the one the card quotes and misses the other leaves a second empty menu row on the same published page, and the page would still be wrong in exactly the way this card exists to end.

**Regenerate, never hand-edit.** Touching fixtures moves `examples/schema-catalog/src/index.ts`. Use the repo's generator and show its `--check` green — and run it on the **untouched** tree first so you can tell your diff from pre-existing drift.

**Reverse verification.** Predict RED and observe it: an assertion that no menubar item carries an array-valued `shortcut`, and that every separator uses the declared boolean spelling, must fail before your change and pass after. Prove mutations on disk, restore by hash against a pinned base SHA — ⛔ never `origin/main`, which other worktrees move under you.

⚠️ **One instrument warning, learned on the sibling card this round.** A census shaped like the demos misses nested occurrences: on objectui#6494 the card said two, this seat said three, and a recursive walk found **four**. Walk the structure, do not grep the shape you expect.

**Fence and hygiene.**
- Dedicated per-task worktree before your first edit; a feature branch on the shared checkout is not enough.
- ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack lives in the common git directory, shared across every worktree, and a `pop` restores another agent's work while reporting success.
- ⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`.
- Claim first: assign yourself and post a claim comment with your session ID and branch. The card will be **unassigned** when you arrive — that is this lane's expected state, not an error, and it does not mean someone else holds it.
- **Run tests narrowly** — the shared validation lock is a cross-agent resource and a wide run has been measured holding it nearly eighteen minutes.

Report your exact file face. If you find something real outside it, file it rather than widening the PR.
